## 固定收益開盤主論述

7月生產者物價顯示能源衝擊正在減弱，投資人因此下修聯準會再次升息的預期，帶動美國公債在8月13日全線上漲；但政府標售30年期公債所付出的殖利率仍創25年新高。2年期殖利率下跌5.9個基點至4.143%，5年期下跌6.6個基點至4.317%，10年期下跌5.1個基點至4.644%，30年期則下跌4.5個基點至5.215%。

這波全面漲勢取代前一交易日各期限表現明顯分化的格局，但貨幣政策風險與承接長天期供給的成本仍有清楚區別。2s10s曲線陡峭化0.8個基點至50.1個基點，2s30s則擴大1.4個基點至107.2個基點。相較1個月前，2年期殖利率低14.2個基點，30年期卻仍高10.9個基點。市場雖調降聯準會即將緊縮的機率，卻未撤除對財政赤字、通膨不確定性及AI建設融資需求擴張所要求的溢價。

7月生產者物價指數較前月持平，年增率由6月的5.5%降至4.7%；核心生產者物價月增0.2%、年增4.2%。能源價格下跌3.1%，連續第2個月下降；食品價格創今年初以來最大跌幅，運輸與倉儲成本則下滑1.8%，為2023年4月以來最大降幅。這份數據延續前一日消費者通膨放緩及7月就業報告轉弱的訊號，使市場隱含的9月升息機率降至40%以下。

但細項並非全面呈現通膨降溫。投資組合管理費與醫院門診服務價格大幅上漲，電子零組件及配件較去年同期貴近28%，電腦設備價格更創下9.8%的紀錄漲幅。克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack在7月會議主張升息25個基點並投下反對票；她表示，自己仍不確信通膨會充分放緩，並再次要求立即採取行動。里奇蒙聯準銀行總裁Tom Barkin則主張維持利率不變，但承認揮之不去的價格壓力最終仍可能迫使聯準會回應。

市場收盤結果較支持耐心觀望。10年期實質殖利率下跌4.5個基點至2.385%，幾乎解釋全部名目殖利率跌幅；10年期損益兩平通膨率僅下滑0.6個基點至2.259%。這項組合顯示，當日行情主要反映市場重新評估未來實質政策與成長路徑，而非全面撤除對長期通膨的補償。

油價下跌也支持這項解讀。WTI下跌2.33%至$81.33，布蘭特原油下跌2.10%至$87.11，中斷先前因中東干擾持續而再起的漲勢。股市正面看待價格壓力放緩及聯準會不再急於行動的組合：標普500指數上漲0.65%並創新高，Nasdaq 100上漲1.15%。美元指數變動不大，下跌0.09%。

財政部標售$250億長債，使行情增添複雜性，但未扭轉公債漲勢。得標殖利率為5.216%，略高於標售前市場殖利率，也是2001年以來30年期標售的最高融資利率。投標倍數為2.39倍，接近前6次同類標售的2.36倍均值，顯示在高殖利率下仍有承接需求。這並非一次失敗的標售，而是成本高昂的均衡：溫和的通膨數據可以壓低當日殖利率，但政府要釋出長天期債券，仍須提供歷史高檔的補償。

## 生產者物價讓聯準會有更多觀望時間

7月PPI是連續第2份支持聯準會在9月會議按兵不動的通膨報告。整體年增率4.7%仍遠高於聯準會目標，但相較6月的5.5%，降幅大於經濟學家預期。伊朗戰爭及荷莫茲海峽正常航運中斷，一度引發能源成本將廣泛傳導至生產與配送環節的疑慮，因此月增率持平格外重要。

能源、食品及貨運相關成本回落，顯示最初的衝擊不再於7月生產流程中加劇。能源價格較6月下跌3.1%，運輸與倉儲成本下降1.8%；扣除食品與能源的加工中間財價格，則創去年11月以來最小漲幅。批發與零售貿易利潤率在6月上升後也小幅回落，有限度顯示企業當月並未加快轉嫁關稅成本。

會納入個人消費支出物價指數的若干項目則表現不一，並非一致溫和。投資組合管理費創1年多來最大漲幅，醫院門診價格也明顯上升；醫師服務與住院醫療價格較受抑制，機票價格則創2025年初以來最大跌幅。因此，花旗、摩根士丹利及Jefferies的經濟學家預測，8月26日公布的7月核心PCE物價將月增0.2%。

資料中心投資循環仍是另一項價格壓力來源。電子零組件及配件價格較去年同期上漲近28%，接近紀錄漲幅；電腦及電腦設備上漲9.8%，創歷來最大年增幅。這些項目過度集中，不足以扭轉7月整體通膨放緩，但說明即使能源及運輸成本下降，資本支出熱潮仍可能在設備市場製造通膨。

利率市場的反應呈現出兩股力量的平衡。短期合約已不再完全反映聯準會2026年內升息；9月行動的機率由本週稍早約50%降至40%以下，但12月合約仍隱含約23個基點的緊縮幅度。投資人不再把今年升息視為必然，而是認為可能性仍高，惟須取決於下一批就業與通膨數據。

Hammack不同意這項重新定價。她表示，近期較低的通膨數據雖值得歡迎，卻不足以讓她確信物價漲幅會繼續放緩至足以回到2%，並重申聯準會應立即採取行動。她延續7月異議的核心立場：支持升息25個基點，認為政策限制性不足，且最終可能需要不只一次調整，但未指明終點利率。

Barkin對眼前決策的看法相反。他認為通膨下降的跡象支持維持利率不變，同時承認部分價格壓力可能固化，之後仍須緊縮。兩人的差異不在於通膨是否仍過高，而在於近期改善是否足以支持等待更多證據，或等待本身會使政策落後情勢。

現任高盛副董事長、前達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Robert Kaplan也主張保留9月決策的彈性。他認為，關稅、油價、勞動力限制及AI建設帶來的通膨壓力，正與科技應用及中國工業產能過剩所產生的通縮力量相互抗衡。在他看來，主席Kevin Warsh應利用傑克森霍爾研討會說明7月維持利率不變的理由，但不應預先承諾9月的結果。

因此，下一次決策取決於改善能否持久且擴及更多項目，而非只看整體PPI。7月數據顯示，先前能源價格飆升對生產者成本的影響正在消退，對關稅敏感的利潤率也未加速上升；但服務投入、科技設備價格及中東持續受阻的廣泛後果仍未釐清。最新一週初領失業救濟金人數上升但仍處低檔，未在前一週疲弱的就業數據之外提供明確的衰退訊號。

## 長債順利標出，代價卻創歷史高檔

財政部30年期公債標售顯示，即使需求有序，市場要求的殖利率也已大幅提高。這筆$250億標售的得標殖利率為5.216%，較紐約時間下午1時截止前的市場殖利率高不到0.5個基點。這項輕微尾差顯示需求僅略遜於標售前水準，2.39倍的投標倍數則稍高於前6次標售的平均值。

這次標售之前，財政部剛完成$420億10年期公債標售，其融資利率創2007年以來同期限新高。兩筆交易共同顯示，投資人願意承接政府按計畫釋出的長天期供給，但前提是殖利率先經歷大幅重定價。30年期融資利率為財政部2001年停止發行長債以來最高；財政部直到2005年才恢復發行。

標售結果公布前後，次級市場仍維持強勢。30年期殖利率收盤下跌約4.5個基點至5.215%，20年期以上美債指數上漲0.61%。交易集中於最直接受到通膨報告與標售影響的期限：FINRA記錄顯示，期限超過7年、但不超過10年的名目附息債券面額成交量為$2,303億，較週三增加25.8%；期限超過20年的成交量為$1,131億，增加34.3%。這些數據衡量雙向成交，仍足以顯示殖利率收低背後的調整規模。

長端未能出現更大漲勢，根源仍在融資供給，而不只是下一次聯準會會議。美國公債在外流通額自2018年以來增加一倍，達約$31兆。本財政年度迄今公債利息支出達$1.17兆，較去年同期增加15%。Fitch維持美國主權債AA+評級，並警告減稅與關稅退稅將使2026年財政赤字相對經濟產出的比重擴大。

財政部最新融資措辭的變化，引發市場揣測官員最終可能縮減長債標售規模。該部不再提評估未來增加附息債與浮動利率債券發行，改稱未來可能調整發行。目前尚未宣布減量，週四標售也依原定金額進行。即使將發行轉向2至7年期公債，也只是轉移融資需求，並未將其消除。

當日殖利率曲線的變化反映這項未解負擔。投資人調降聯準會預期緊縮幅度後，5年期殖利率跌幅大於30年期，使2s30s達107.2個基點，較1個月前陡峭25.1個基點。標售獲得足夠承接，但並未證明在赤字仍龐大、央行不再是主要邊際買家的情況下，投資人願意把長期殖利率鎖定在顯著低於5%的水準。

聯準會另對短期融資環境表達信心。紐約聯準銀行表示，在截至9月14日的每月操作期間內，不會進行任何準備金管理用途的國庫券購買；這是自2025年12月開始此類購買以來首次暫停，但仍計畫進行約$170億再投資買進。

暫停購買反映現金充裕，並非貨幣政策改變，也不是重啟量化緊縮。8月12日擔保隔夜融資利率為3.62%，較準備金餘額利率低3個基點；8月5日銀行準備金為$3兆，高於2025年底的$2.85兆。即使財政部增加國庫券發行，貨幣市場基金資產仍處紀錄高檔。融資市場因此讓聯準會有空間暫停額外的準備金管理買進，但長端仍要求存續期間與財政風險溢價。

## 日本更接近升息，其他央行選擇等待

日本釋出海外市場最強的新一波緊縮訊號。據知情人士透露，首相高市早苗領導的政府支持日本央行近期升息，時間可能落在9月或10月。政府希望強化7月底美日匯市干預的效果，與日本央行擔心日圓再度走弱推升進口物價的考量逐漸一致。

首相辦公室表示，具體政策決定仍由日本央行負責，維持央行獨立性的正式界線。不過，官員在7月會議前已表達支持總裁植田和男提出更偏鷹派的評估。日本央行決策者仍在評估經濟與物價，尚未就行動時點作出最終決定。

生產者物價則強化採取行動的理由。日本7月企業物價指數年增7.2%，僅略低於上修後的6月7.3%，仍是2023年3月以來最快增速；月增率為0.1%，6月增幅則修正為0.5%。石油與煤炭製品、化學品及非鐵金屬是年增主力。

成本壓力愈來愈難由中小企業吸收。帝國數據銀行記錄顯示，2026年上半年有556家企業因無法轉嫁投入成本上升而破產，創2018年開始統計以來最高的半年紀錄；僅7月就有121件，亦創單月新高。燃料及原物料成本上升、AI帶動機械與金屬需求、薪資壓力及日圓疲弱，都是推升因素。

市場原已反映日本央行在9月18日決策會議升息的機率達74%，因此政府支持升息的報導對匯率影響有限。日圓一度升至接近159.18兌1美元，但日本交易時段收在約159.50，創7月30日以來最弱收盤，並接近過去曾引發干預的水準。日本10年期公債殖利率微升至2.87%，接近7月創下的30年高點。

匯率反應平淡，使市場焦點由日本央行是否再次升息，轉向升息後的政策步調。日本政策利率為1%，相較之下，聯準會目標區間為3.5%至3.75%。單次升息只能小幅縮小利差；但若在12個月內第3度升息，已會是日本央行自1989年以來最快的緊縮速度。政府與央行須在支撐日圓，以及6月家庭支出連續第7個月下降之間取得平衡。

挪威選擇等待。挪威央行連續第2次會議把存款利率維持在4.25%，符合全部16名分析師的預測，同時保留再次升息的可能。總裁Ida Wolden Bache表示，決策者一致認為近期通膨數據尚不足以證明展望出現重大變化，需要更多時間評估資訊。

這項決定是在兩份意外溫和的核心通膨數據之後作出，但薪資成長及緊俏的勞動市場仍支撐國內價格壓力。隔夜交換市場將9月前反映的緊縮幅度由15個基點降至12個基點，年底前則由27個基點降至22個基點。Danske Bank仍預測，若8月核心通膨回升至3%以上，央行將於9月升息，但也形容這會是相當接近的決定。

土耳其央行並未改變實際政策立場，而是把預測向市場預期靠攏。總裁Fatih Karahan將年底通膨預測由26%上調至28%，更接近央行7月調查的29%預期，並承認先前預測有部分未能達成。7月年通膨已放緩至31.8%，但伊朗衝突以及油、天然氣與食品價格波動，仍推高這個高度依賴進口能源經濟體的通膨展望。

央行繼續以40%的隔夜利率提供資金，而不是37%的1週附買回利率，維持戰爭爆發後採取的事實上緊縮措施。Karahan表示，央行仍考慮恢復以1週附買回操作供應資金，但須視市場情況而定。用於描述可能結果的通膨預測與政策目標不同；通膨目標仍為24%，2027年的預測與目標則同為15%。

澳洲的證據顯示，先前升息正透過住宅市場抑制經濟活動。澳洲央行助理總裁Chris Kent表示，房價下跌正在收緊金融環境，因而減少原本可能需要額外施加的限制。7月全國房價下跌0.7%，雪梨跌幅1.4%居首；6月至7月的合計跌幅為2022年12月以來最大。

Kent仍形容通膨風險明顯偏向上行，並表示包括荷莫茲海峽在合理時間內恢復通航等多項條件，都必須朝有利方向發展，通膨才會如預測般放緩。澳洲央行今年已升息3次，最近一次會議則按兵不動。其基準展望預期通膨將回到接近目標，但總裁Michele Bullock仍保留在物價高於該路徑時進一步緊縮的可能。

英國公布的是較強勁的成長結果，而非政策決定。6月產出增加0.3%，帶動第2季GDP成長0.4%，上半年則成長1%。企業投資第2季增加1.7%，資訊與通訊產業支撐服務業。經濟學家警告，世界盃支出及異常溫暖天氣的效應將會消退，下半年還將面臨公用事業費率上升、金融環境緊縮及勞動市場轉弱的壓力。

## AI借款範圍擴大，再融資壓力同步加深

企業市場持續為AI資本支出循環供應資金，但同一波借款潮也開始改變高評級信用債的相對價值。超微半導體以公司歷來最大規模的美元債券發行籌得$47.5億，共發行4檔、期限介於3至10年。最長一檔的定價由初步討論水準收窄約25個基點，最終為美國公債殖利率加90個基點。

AMD表示，募集資金可用於一般公司用途，包括償還債務。公司有$8.75億債券將於9月到期；截至6月27日，債務為$32億，現金及短期投資為$131億。隨著這家晶片製造商擴大與Anthropic及微軟等客戶的協議，分析師預估今年營收將成長47%，超過$510億。

這筆交易同時反映投資人的承接能力及未來供給規模。AMD是週四進場的3家投資等級發行人之一；科技公司及資料中心開發商則持續增加傳統債券、擔保專案債務及租賃義務。供給已不再局限於最大型超大規模雲端業者，也不只存在於這些公司的資產負債表。

Zenith Arc是Fluidstack與Next Frontier在奧克拉荷馬州成立的資料中心合資企業，推出$22.5億綠色債券，背後資產是一座出租給Jane Street子公司的設施。這批5年期、Ba2評級的優先擔保票據，擬用於興建運算中心及一座可支援約149百萬瓦容量的變電站。15年租約除基本租金外，還要求承租人負擔營運成本、稅款、公用事業費、保險及電力費用，並由Jane Street Group提供市場慣常的擔保。

這項結構以長期合約付款現金流支撐一個仍面臨施工、電力及科技風險的專案，也把資料中心的融資管道拓展至超大規模雲端業者債券之外。Edged Compute今年已發行$13億綠色債務，TeraWulf則取得$32億融資。資料中心專案的永續債券發行額，已由2024年的$76億增至2025年的$112億。

租賃承諾又增添一層無法由傳統債務總額完全反映的義務。高盛分析師估計，超大規模雲端業者約有$2,000億租賃已列入公開財務報表，另有約$1兆尚未起租的租賃義務揭露於附註中；後者不到1個月前仍為$7,250億。這些合約涉及尚未可供使用的容量，因此還未以營業租賃資產與負債列入資產負債表。

供給增加也影響未直接涉足AI的企業。法國巴黎銀行發現，高評級科技業借款人對資金的競爭，正推升部分傳統防禦型歐洲企業的信用違約交換成本。LVMH、Sanofi及BAE Systems等借款人的CDS利差，自2025年底以來已擴大逾10%；同期間整體高評級CDS指數仍接近近20年最窄水準。

法國巴黎銀行將此形容為一種收斂現象：超大規模雲端業者競逐同一批高品質資金，使原本極窄的個別企業利差向指數均值靠攏。全球投資等級公司債利差約為80個基點，只比金融危機後低點高約6個基點。因此，龐大發債量可能先重定價最安全的企業債，之後才在主要指數形成明顯利差擴大。

在美債上漲之際，當日掛牌信用產品仍有正向表現。投資等級債基金LQD上漲0.41%，HYG上漲0.23%，JNK上漲0.20%。這些價格變化包含基準殖利率下跌的影響，無法單獨反映信用風險，但顯示發債量增加並未引發廣泛避險。AMD的定價也證明，資本實力雄厚的科技業借款人仍可較初步條件大幅收窄利差。

市政融資則提供另一個例子，顯示投資人願意承擔結構型信用風險以取得額外收益。截至8月13日，證券化可負擔住宅債券已透過37筆交易發行$45億，不僅超過2025年全年的$34億，也遠高於此結構於2019年初次出現時的$7.14億。

這類證券匯集多處可負擔公寓資產的抵押貸款，讓貸款機構能回收資金並承作新貸款。National Finance Authority在7月發行$1.623億憑證，背後權益來自分布於10州的21筆抵押貸款，認購需求超額。許多此類交易具有投資等級中段評級，殖利率卻可媲美評級較低的市政債類別；部分原因是其3%或4%的票息，相較5%結構較難吸引傳統散戶及獨立管理帳戶。

但並非所有借款人都能順利進入初級市場。Telesat在逾$20億債務接近到期之際取得$1.2億定期貸款，但旗下傳統地球同步衛星業務第2季營收下滑25%，並錄得C$1,270萬營業虧損，股價下跌13.4%。

Telesat GEO在12月須償還定期貸款$13.2億及優先擔保票據$3.87億，之後還有2027年6月到期的擔保票據$2.25億，以及2027年10月到期的無擔保票據$2.13億。目前現金流與準備金不足以支付這些債務。公司已與貸款機構顧問討論再融資9個月，管理階層表示預期會處理到期債務，但同時警告，這項不確定性已使GEO業務能否履行義務存在重大疑慮。

烏克蘭鐵路公司正準備另一項重整方案；此前政府已允許自8月初起把貨運費率提高30%。這家國營營運商有$11億債券，1月停止支付利息，並未能償還7月到期的約$7億債務。4月談判未達成協議後，與債權人的正式協商仍未重啟。

調高費率有助提升營收潛力，但仍低於公司要求的45%。公司另提議於2027年1月再調高15%，目前尚未獲准。先前的重整方案包括削減本金20%、把期限延長至2033年、按期攤還，並讓票息逐步上升；債權回收也有一部分與貨運量連結。運量下滑、基礎設施遭攻擊，以及人力、能源與維修成本增加，仍是修訂方案的主要限制。

巴西鋼鐵製造商CSN在推動資產出售及爭取展延到期債務之際，連續第10季虧損。第2季調整後虧損達7.73億巴西里亞爾，接近去年同期的6倍；淨負債升至421億巴西里亞爾，相當於息稅折舊攤銷前獲利的3.49倍。債券持有人已批准一筆$10億換債，潛在買家也已對水泥業務提出報價，但槓桿率上升顯示，這些措施尚未修復資產負債表。

## 本地融資變化帶來新買家與新限制

數個新興市場改變的是國內融資結構，而不只是調整政策利率。越南出現最迫切的失衡：在政府要求銀行支持兩位數經濟成長之際，越南盾貸款已比存款高出約2,000兆越南盾，相當於$768億。

越南國家銀行警告，這項資金缺口會對流動性、利率及金融穩定構成風險。總理Le Minh Hung仍要求政策利率維持不變、增加市場流動性、降低銀行資金成本，並實質調降貸款利率。銀行也接獲指示，對符合資格的中小企業提供貸款時，利率須至少比各銀行相同期限平均利率低1個百分點。

彼此衝突的政策要求日益難以兼顧。政府為達成全年目標，尋求下半年經濟成長近12%；但7月消費者通膨為4.45%，年初貿易逆差也增加外幣需求。央行的信用成長目標約為15%，卻表示通膨、外部波動及銀行籌資能力限制了貨幣政策的支持空間。Techcombank啟動$10億聯貸案，更凸顯銀行轉向境外融資。

奈及利亞把央行公開市場操作證券的投資人範圍，由銀行擴大至個人、企業及非銀行金融機構。央行也恢復4至90天期附買回操作，並取消參與外匯與政府公債標售者使用貼現窗口的限制。新架構立即生效，未來OMO規模與期限將取決於流動性及政策目標。

Rand Merchant Bank預期，這些工具開放給與國庫券相同的投資人群體後，OMO殖利率將下降，與國庫券利率的差距也會逐步縮小；國內投資人同時多了一項有收益、可取代股票的選擇。這項調整既擴大央行證券的承接管道，也恢復透過定期附買回操作注入流動性的彈性。

斯里蘭卡則朝拉長到期結構的方向調整，降低對外債及短天期國內國庫券的依賴，同時增加較長天期的本地債券。財政部副部長Anil Jayantha Fernando表示，收入比計畫高約15%，政府仍有望達成2026年赤字目標，但貨幣貶值正在推高支出。官員也在考慮日後發行浮動利率、通膨連結及綠色債券。

智利則正為公司債創造一個規模可觀的新買家。公共退休金支持基金FAPP預計未來5年籌集約$40億，至2036年達$140億，其中約三分之二將投向智利公司固定收益資產。相較當地約102兆智利披索、即$1,120億的公司債市場，這項配置規模相當大。

隨著2025年改革提高雇主提撥比率，私人退休金資產也在增加。截至6月止的12個月內，資產增加35.2兆智利披索至234.4兆。FAPP截至3月持有3,779億智利披索，全部投資於固定收益證券，並預期公司債最終將取代其大部分主權債配置。這項潛在需求可為當地發行人提供結構性資金來源，而非只是對每日利率變動的短期反應。

印尼央行的人事任命同樣有助政策延續，但財政考驗仍未解決。總統Prabowo Subianto提名副總裁Aida S. Budiman出任資深副總裁，並提名執行董事Solikin M. Juhro及M. Anwar Bashori出任副總裁；此前，他已選定代理總裁Destry Damayanti為印尼央行總裁的唯一候選人。

任用央行內部資深官員，降低Perry Warjiyo離任後的不確定性，印尼10年期公債殖利率週四早盤下跌2個基點，觸及1個月低點。人事案仍須國會批准，聽證預計下週開始。這些任命並未解決央行如何在穩定印尼盾與政府要求加快成長之間取得平衡，尤其新法已把央行職責擴大至促進永續經濟發展。

## 後續市場意義

聯準會接下來的考驗，是7月生產者物價帶來的舒緩能否延續至9月會議前的其餘數據。核心PCE將於8月26日公布，多家銀行的經濟學家預測月增0.2%。其中服務項目將決定能源、貨運及貿易利潤率下降的同時，價格放緩是否已充分擴大；後續就業報告也須釐清7月招聘轉弱究竟是持續趨勢還是暫時現象。

Warsh在8月稍晚的傑克森霍爾演說，將決定聯準會如何整合這些證據。若他為7月維持利率不變辯護，並強調累積改善，市場對9月升息機率的下修將獲得支持；若更著重通膨仍高於目標、科技相關價格壓力或等待的風險，即使美債已上漲，Hammack的主張仍會保有分量。市場已不再確信今年一定會升息，因此聯準會溝通仍足以同時改變9月機率及12月政策路徑。

油價是通膨降溫論述最直接的外部挑戰。週四WTI下跌2.33%、布蘭特原油下跌2.10%，有助緩和近期壓力，但美國與伊朗尚未達成恢復荷莫茲海峽正常航運的協議。若船舶持續通行、運費與保險成本下降，7月能源及運輸價格的跌勢將更為持久；若攻擊再起、干擾延續或原油再度上漲，能源影響生產者成本、損益兩平通膨率及央行決策的傳導管道就會恢復。

財政部本輪標售週期已經結束，但融資問題仍在。30年期公債以5.216%標出，顯示此一水準有足夠需求，卻不代表投資人會以顯著較低的殖利率承接相同期限的供給。未來若調整標售規模，仍須連同整體融資需求、擴大的財政赤字及轉移至較短期限的發行量一併評估。過去1個月2s30s陡峭化25.1個基點，使長端同時容易受到預算政策及下一次通膨反彈影響。

日本9月18日的決策是最明確的海外政策事件。政府支持近期升息、生產者物價上漲7.2%，以及日圓接近160，都強化採取行動的理由。接下來要看日本央行會把一次升息描述為已足夠，還是暗示更快的政策路徑，以更持久地縮小利差。家庭支出疲弱及過度緊縮風險仍是制衡因素。

更迫切的亞洲主權債考驗，是印尼8月14日的預算演說。投資人將觀察赤字能否可信地控制在法定3%上限以內，以及融資條件是否符合財政紀律。低於2.5%的赤字會獲得正面看待；CIMB估計，若赤字為2.2%，即使較重的到期壓力使2027年總發債額增加1.4%至1,750兆印尼盾，淨發債額仍可降至722兆印尼盾。收入假設、免費餐食計畫成本，以及是否動用國營銀行資產負債表，將決定這份計畫能否延續印尼債券近期的改善。

公司信用市場的關鍵，在於AI融資是否仍集中於現金充裕或有合約支撐的發行人，抑或開始更積極地重定價整體高評級市場。AMD的$47.5億債券在行銷期間收窄利差，Zenith Arc則把Jane Street的長期租約帶入專案債券市場。接下來的交易將檢驗，這些條件能否繼續抵銷傳統債務、擔保債券及尚未起租義務的供給擴張。

財務受壓借款人則面臨更具體的期限。Telesat必須在無法依賴GEO業務現金流的情況下，為12月到期債務再融資或進行重整。烏克蘭鐵路公司在未支付利息與本金後，須把30%的貨運費率調升轉化為債權人方案；額外調升費率尚未獲准，也使未來收入仍附帶條件。兩家公司雖分別透過新資金爭取時間或改善營運基礎，但最終債務條款及損失分配仍未解決。

overall_summary.headline: 生產者物價降溫推升美債，但長債仍以25年最高殖利率標出
overall_summary.session_narrative:
8月13日美國公債全線收高：2年期殖利率下跌5.9個基點至4.143%，5年期下跌6.6個基點至4.317%，10年期下跌5.1個基點至4.644%，30年期則下跌4.5個基點至5.215%。7月生產者物價較前月持平、年增4.7%，低於6月的5.5%；核心價格月增0.2%、年增4.2%。能源、食品及運輸成本下降，使市場隱含的9月升息機率降至40%以下。

這波漲勢主要反映市場重新評估未來實質政策與成長路徑：10年期實質殖利率下跌4.5個基點，損益兩平通膨率僅下滑0.6個基點。油價走低進一步支持這項解讀，但部分服務及科技設備價格大幅上升，使通膨訊號仍顯分歧。

財政部$250億30年期公債標售的得標殖利率為5.216%，創2001年以來同類標售最高融資利率；不過尾差輕微、投標倍數達2.39倍，顯示市場仍有承接需求。這是一次有序、但成本處於歷史高檔的標售；即使通膨降溫降低聯準會立即行動的壓力，長端仍暴露於財政赤字及融資供給風險。
overall_summary.summary: 7月生產者通膨降溫，降低近期聯準會緊縮預期並帶動各期限殖利率下滑；但$250億30年期公債仍須以5.216%標出，存續期間、財政風險及龐大融資需求的溢價因而延續。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied across the curve on Aug. 13 after July producer prices showed the energy shock losing force, allowing investors to reduce expectations for another Federal Reserve increase even as the government paid a quarter-century-high yield to sell 30-year debt. The 2-year yield fell 5.9 basis points to 4.143%, the 5-year declined 6.6 basis points to 4.317%, the 10-year eased 5.1 basis points to 4.644% and the 30-year dropped 4.5 basis points to 5.215%.

The rally replaced the previous session’s sharp maturity divide with broad relief, but it did not erase the distinction between monetary-policy risk and the cost of absorbing long-duration supply. The 2s10s curve steepened 0.8 basis point to 50.1 basis points, while 2s30s widened 1.4 basis points to 107.2 basis points. Over one month, the 2-year yield was 14.2 basis points lower, but the 30-year remained 10.9 basis points higher. Investors marked down the probability of imminent Fed tightening without withdrawing the premium attached to deficits, inflation uncertainty and the expanding financing demands of the artificial-intelligence buildout.

The producer-price index was unchanged in July and increased 4.7% from a year earlier, down from 5.5% in June. Core producer prices rose 0.2% on the month and 4.2% over 12 months. Energy prices declined 3.1% for a second monthly fall, food prices registered their largest drop since the start of the year, and transportation and warehousing costs fell 1.8%, the most since April 2023. The result reinforced the previous day’s moderation in consumer inflation and the weaker July employment report, driving the market-implied probability of a September rate increase below 40%.

The details were not uniformly disinflationary. Portfolio-management fees and hospital outpatient care rose sharply, while electronic components and accessories were almost 28% more expensive than a year earlier and computer-equipment prices increased a record 9.8%. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, who dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase at the July meeting, said she still lacked confidence that inflation would slow sufficiently and again called for action now. Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin instead made the case for holding steady while acknowledging that lingering price pressure could eventually force a response.

The completed market outcome favored patience. The 10-year real yield fell 4.5 basis points to 2.385%, accounting for nearly all of the nominal yield decline, while the 10-year breakeven slipped only 0.6 basis point to 2.259%. That composition indicated that the session was principally a reassessment of the expected real policy and growth path rather than a wholesale removal of longer-term inflation compensation.

Lower oil prices supported that reading. WTI fell 2.33% to $81.33 and Brent declined 2.10% to $87.11, interrupting the renewed advance associated with the continuing disruption in the Middle East. Equities treated the combination of softer prices and a less urgent Fed as constructive: the S&P 500 rose 0.65% to a record, and the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.15%. The dollar index was little changed, down 0.09%.

Treasury’s $25 billion long-bond sale complicated but did not overturn the rally. The auction stopped at 5.216%, slightly above the prevailing pre-auction yield and the highest borrowing rate for a 30-year sale since 2001. A 2.39 bid-to-cover ratio, close to the 2.36 average for the previous six comparable auctions, showed that demand remained available at elevated yields. The message was less a failed auction than a costly equilibrium: benign inflation could lower yields on the day, while the government still needed to offer historically high compensation to place duration.

## Producer Prices Give the Fed More Time

July PPI supplied a second consecutive inflation report consistent with waiting at the September meeting. The 4.7% annual headline rate remained far above the Fed’s objective, but the decline from 5.5% in June was larger than economists had expected. The unchanged monthly reading was particularly important after the Iran war and interruption of normal traffic through the Strait of Hormuz had raised concern that energy costs would spread more broadly through production and distribution.

The retreat in energy, food and freight-related costs showed that the initial shock was no longer intensifying across the July production pipeline. Energy prices fell 3.1% from June, and transportation and warehousing costs dropped 1.8%. Prices for processed intermediate goods excluding food and energy registered their smallest increase since November. Wholesale and retail trade margins also edged lower after rising in June, providing limited evidence that companies were not accelerating the pass-through of tariff costs during the month.

Several components feeding into the personal-consumption-expenditures price indexes were mixed rather than uniformly benign. Portfolio-management fees posted their largest increase in more than a year, and hospital outpatient prices also rose strongly. Physician services and inpatient hospital care were restrained, while airfares recorded their largest decline since early 2025. Economists at Citigroup, Morgan Stanley and Jefferies consequently projected a 0.2% increase in July core PCE prices, due Aug. 26.

The data-center investment cycle remained a separate source of price pressure. Electronic components and accessories cost nearly 28% more than a year earlier, close to a record increase, and computers and computer equipment rose 9.8%, the largest annual advance on record. Those categories are too concentrated to reverse the broader July moderation, but they demonstrate that the capital-spending boom can create inflation in equipment markets even as energy and transportation costs recede.

The rates response reflected the balance. Short-term contracts no longer fully priced a Fed increase during 2026. The probability of a September move fell to less than 40%, from about 50% earlier in the week, while the December contract still implied approximately 23 basis points of tightening. Investors therefore shifted from treating an increase this year as certain to regarding it as highly possible but dependent on the next employment and inflation releases.

Hammack resisted that repricing. The Cleveland Fed president said the latest lower inflation figures were welcome but did not give her confidence that price growth would continue falling far enough to return to 2%. She repeated that the Fed should act immediately. Her position retained the substance of her July dissent: she favored a quarter-point increase, considered policy insufficiently restrictive and believed more than one adjustment might ultimately be required, while declining to specify the final rate.

Barkin took the other side of the immediate decision. The Richmond Fed president argued that signs of declining inflation supported holding rates steady, while allowing that some price pressure could become embedded and later require tightening. The distinction between the two officials was not over whether inflation remained excessive. It was whether the recent improvement justified waiting for more evidence or represented a delay that could leave policy behind the curve.

Former Dallas Fed President Robert Kaplan, now a Goldman Sachs vice chairman, also favored preserving flexibility through September. He described inflationary pressure from tariffs, oil, labor constraints and the AI buildout as operating against disinflation from technology adoption and Chinese industrial overcapacity. In his view, Chair Kevin Warsh should use the Jackson Hole symposium to explain the reasoning behind July’s hold without committing the Fed to a predetermined September outcome.

The next decision consequently depends on the durability and breadth of the improvement rather than the headline PPI result alone. July showed that the earlier energy surge was fading from producer costs and that tariff-sensitive margins were not accelerating. It also left service inputs, technology equipment and the wider consequences of the continuing Middle East disruption unresolved. Applications for unemployment benefits rose in the latest week but remained low, adding no clear recession signal to last week’s weaker employment figures.

## The Long Bond Clears, but at a Historic Cost

Treasury’s 30-year auction demonstrated how far the market’s required yield has risen even when demand is orderly. The $25 billion sale stopped at 5.216%, less than half a basis point above the yield immediately before the 1 p.m. New York deadline. That small tail indicated demand fell only slightly short of the pre-auction level, while the 2.39 bid-to-cover ratio was marginally stronger than the six-auction average.

The sale followed a $42 billion 10-year auction that had produced the highest financing rate for that maturity since 2007. Together, the transactions showed that investors would absorb the government’s scheduled duration, but only after a substantial reset in yields. The 30-year borrowing rate was the highest since the Treasury discontinued long-bond issuance in 2001, before restoring it in 2005.

Secondary trading remained firm around the result. The 30-year yield ended about 4.5 basis points lower at 5.215%, while the 20-year-and-longer Treasury index gained 0.61%. Activity was concentrated in the maturities most directly affected by the inflation report and auction: FINRA recorded $230.3 billion of par trading in nominal coupons longer than 7 years and no more than 10 years, up 25.8% from Wednesday, and $113.1 billion in maturities longer than 20 years, up 34.3%. Those figures measure two-way turnover, but they show the scale of adjustment behind the lower closing yields.

The long end’s resistance to a larger rally remains rooted in financing supply rather than the next Fed meeting alone. Treasuries outstanding have doubled since 2018 to about $31 trillion. Interest on the public debt reached $1.17 trillion in the fiscal year to date, 15% more than in the comparable period, while Fitch retained the sovereign’s AA+ rating and warned that the fiscal deficit would widen relative to economic output in 2026 because of tax cuts and tariff rebates.

Treasury’s latest borrowing language has encouraged speculation that officials could eventually reduce long-bond auction sizes. The department replaced a reference to evaluating future increases in coupon and floating-rate issuance with the broader possibility of future changes. No reduction has been announced, and Thursday’s sale proceeded at the scheduled amount. Shifting issuance toward 2- to 7-year notes would also relocate the borrowing requirement rather than eliminate it.

The session’s curve move captured that unresolved burden. The 5-year yield fell more than the 30-year as investors reduced the expected amount of Fed tightening, leaving 2s30s at 107.2 basis points, 25.1 basis points steeper than a month earlier. The auction was adequately covered, but it did not establish that investors were prepared to lock in long yields below 5% while deficits remain large and the central bank is no longer a major marginal buyer.

The Fed separately signaled confidence in short-term funding conditions. The New York Fed said it would make no reserve-management purchases of Treasury bills during the monthly period ending Sept. 14, the first pause since such buying began in December 2025. It still planned about $17 billion of reinvestment purchases.

The pause reflected abundant cash rather than a change in monetary policy or a restart of quantitative tightening. The Secured Overnight Financing Rate fixed at 3.62% on Aug. 12, 3 basis points below the rate paid on reserve balances, and bank reserves stood at $3 trillion on Aug. 5, up from $2.85 trillion at the end of 2025. Money-market-fund assets were at records even as Treasury increased bill issuance. Funding markets therefore gave the Fed room to suspend additional reserve-management buying while the long end continued to demand a premium for duration and fiscal risk.

## Japan Moves Closer to a Hike as Other Central Banks Wait

Japan produced the strongest fresh overseas tightening signal. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s government was supportive of a near-term Bank of Japan increase, likely in September or October, according to people familiar with the matter. The government’s desire to reinforce the effect of the late-July US-Japan currency intervention was aligning with the BOJ’s concern that renewed yen weakness would raise import prices.

The Prime Minister’s office said specific policy decisions remained the BOJ’s responsibility, preserving the formal boundary around central-bank independence. Officials had nevertheless conveyed support before the July meeting for Governor Kazuo Ueda to present a more hawkish assessment. BOJ policymakers were still evaluating the economy and prices and had not made a final decision on timing.

Producer prices strengthened the case for action. Japan’s corporate-goods price index rose 7.2% in July from a year earlier, only slightly below June’s upwardly revised 7.3%, the fastest pace since March 2023. Prices increased 0.1% on the month after a revised 0.5% rise in June. Oil and coal products, chemicals and nonferrous metals led the annual increase.

The cost pressure has become increasingly difficult for smaller companies to absorb. Teikoku Databank recorded 556 bankruptcies linked to companies’ inability to pass on higher input costs during the first half of 2026, the highest half-year total since its records began in 2018. July alone produced 121 cases, a monthly record. Higher fuel and raw-material costs, AI-related demand for machinery and metals, wage pressure and the weak yen have all contributed.

Markets already assigned a 74% probability to an increase at the BOJ’s Sept. 18 decision, limiting the currency response to reports of government support. The yen briefly strengthened toward 159.18 per dollar but finished the Japanese day near 159.50, its weakest close since July 30 and close to a level that has prompted intervention before. Japan’s 10-year government-bond yield edged up to 2.87%, near the three-decade high reached in July.

The subdued currency response shifted attention from whether the BOJ will deliver the next increase to the pace that follows it. Japan’s policy rate is 1%, compared with the Fed’s 3.5%-to-3.75% target range. A single move would narrow that gap only slightly, while a third increase within 12 months would already represent the BOJ’s fastest tightening pace since 1989. The government and central bank must balance support for the yen against household spending that fell for a seventh straight month in June.

Norway chose to wait. Norges Bank left its deposit rate at 4.25% for a second meeting, matching all 16 analyst forecasts, and retained the possibility of another increase. Governor Ida Wolden Bache said policymakers agreed that the recent inflation data did not yet establish a material change in the outlook and that more time was needed to assess the information.

The decision followed two unexpectedly benign core-inflation readings, but wage growth and a tight labor market continued to support domestic price pressure. Overnight swaps reduced the amount of tightening priced by September to 12 basis points from 15 and by year-end to 22 basis points from 27. Danske Bank continued to forecast a September increase if August core inflation moves back above 3%, although it described the decision as a close call.

Turkey’s central bank moved its forecast toward the market rather than changing its operative stance. Governor Fatih Karahan raised the year-end inflation projection to 28% from 26%, closer to the 29% expectation in the bank’s July survey, and acknowledged a partial failure to meet earlier projections. Annual inflation had slowed to 31.8% in July, but the Iran conflict and volatility in oil, gas and food prices had raised the outlook for an economy heavily dependent on imported energy.

The bank continued to provide funding through its 40% overnight rate rather than its 37% 1-week repo rate, maintaining a de facto tightening introduced after the war began. Karahan said a return to 1-week repo funding remained under consideration but would depend on market conditions. The inflation target, distinct from the forecast used to describe the likely outcome, stayed at 24%; the 2027 forecast and target were both set at 15%.

Australia offered evidence that earlier increases were restraining activity through housing. Reserve Bank Assistant Governor Chris Kent said falling home prices were making financial conditions more restrictive and reducing the amount of additional restraint that might otherwise be needed. Nationwide values fell 0.7% in July, led by a 1.4% decline in Sydney, and the combined June-July fall was the largest since December 2022.

Kent still described inflation risks as tilted strongly upward and said several developments, including a reasonably prompt reopening of Hormuz, would need to go right for inflation to slow as forecast. The RBA has raised rates three times this year and held at its latest meeting. Its central outlook has inflation returning toward target, but Governor Michele Bullock has retained the possibility of further tightening if prices exceed that path.

The UK supplied a firmer growth result rather than a policy decision. Output increased 0.3% in June, helping GDP expand 0.4% in Q2 and 1% over the first half. Business investment rose 1.7% during the quarter, and information and communications supported services. Economists cautioned that World Cup spending and unusually warm weather would fade while higher utility bills, tight financial conditions and a weakening labor market weighed on the second half.

## AI Borrowing Broadens While Refinancing Stress Deepens

Corporate markets continued to finance the AI capital cycle even as the same borrowing wave began to alter relative value in high-grade credit. Advanced Micro Devices raised $4.75 billion in its largest US dollar bond sale, issuing four tranches with maturities from 3 to 10 years. Pricing on the longest tranche tightened by about 25 basis points from initial discussion to 90 basis points over Treasuries.

AMD said proceeds could be used for general corporate purposes, including debt repayment. The company has $875 million of bonds maturing in September and reported $3.2 billion of debt against $13.1 billion of cash and short-term investments as of June 27. Analyst estimates projected revenue to increase 47% this year to more than $51 billion as the chipmaker expands agreements with customers including Anthropic and Microsoft.

The transaction illustrated both investor capacity and the scale of prospective supply. AMD was one of three investment-grade issuers in the market Thursday, while technology companies and data-center developers continued to add conventional bonds, secured project debt and lease obligations. The supply is no longer confined to the largest hyperscalers or to their own balance sheets.

Zenith Arc, an Oklahoma data-center venture between Fluidstack and Next Frontier, brought a $2.25 billion green-bond offering backed by a facility leased to a Jane Street subsidiary. The 5-year senior-secured Ba2 notes were intended to fund construction of the compute center and a substation supporting about 149 megawatts of capacity. The 15-year lease requires the tenant to cover operating costs, taxes, utilities, insurance and power charges in addition to base rent, with a customary guaranty from Jane Street Group.

That structure places a long contractual payment stream behind a project exposed to construction, power and technology risks. It also broadens the funding channel for data centers beyond hyperscaler bonds. Edged Compute had already sold $1.3 billion of green debt this year, while TeraWulf secured $3.2 billion. Sustainable bonds for data-center projects reached $11.2 billion in 2025, up from $7.6 billion in 2024.

Lease commitments add another layer that conventional debt totals do not fully capture. Goldman Sachs analysts estimated that hyperscalers had about $200 billion of leases recognized in public financial statements and roughly $1 trillion of uncommenced lease obligations disclosed in footnotes. The latter figure was up from $725 billion less than a month earlier. These contracts concern capacity that has not yet become available for use and therefore has not entered the balance sheet as an operating lease asset and liability.

The growth of supply is affecting companies with no direct AI exposure. BNP Paribas found that competition for capital from highly rated technology borrowers was pushing credit-default-swap costs higher for some traditionally defensive European companies. CDS spreads for borrowers including LVMH, Sanofi and BAE Systems had risen more than 10% since the end of 2025, even while broad high-grade CDS indexes remained close to their tightest levels in almost 20 years.

BNP described a convergence in which very tight single-name spreads move toward the index average as hyperscalers compete for the same pool of high-quality capital. Global investment-grade corporate-bond spreads were indicated near 80 basis points, approximately 6 basis points above their post-financial-crisis low. Heavy issuance can consequently reprice the safest corporate names before creating an obvious widening in the headline indexes.

The day’s listed credit performance remained constructive alongside the Treasury rally. The LQD investment-grade fund gained 0.41%, HYG rose 0.23% and JNK added 0.20%. Those price changes incorporated lower benchmark yields and do not isolate credit risk, but they showed no broad risk-off response to the increase in issuance. AMD’s pricing also demonstrated that a strongly capitalized technology borrower could tighten substantially from initial terms.

Municipal finance supplied a separate example of investors accepting structured credit for additional yield. Issuance of securitized affordable-housing bonds reached $4.5 billion across 37 deals through Aug. 13, already exceeding the $3.4 billion sold in all of 2025 and far above the $714 million issued when the structure emerged in 2019.

The securities pool mortgages on multiple affordable apartment properties, allowing lenders to recycle capital into new loans. A July offering from the National Finance Authority packaged $162.3 million of certificates backed by interests in 21 mortgages across 10 states and was oversubscribed. Many such deals carry mid-investment-grade ratings but offer yields comparable with lower-rated municipal sectors, partly because their 3% or 4% coupons attract fewer traditional retail and separately managed accounts than 5% structures.

Strong primary-market access did not extend to every borrower. Telesat obtained a $120 million term loan as more than $2 billion of debt approached maturity, but its legacy geostationary-satellite business reported a 25% revenue decline and a C$12.7 million operating loss for Q2. The shares fell 13.4%.

Telesat GEO owes $1.32 billion under a term loan and $387 million of senior secured notes in December, followed by $225 million of secured notes in June 2027 and $213 million of unsecured notes in October 2027. Current cash flow and reserves do not cover those obligations. The company has discussed refinancing with lender advisers for nine months and said management expects to address the maturities, while warning that the uncertainty raises substantial doubt about the GEO business’s ability to meet its obligations.

Ukrainian Railways was preparing another restructuring proposal after the government allowed a 30% freight-tariff increase from the start of August. The state operator has $1.1 billion of bonds, stopped paying interest in January and failed to repay about $700 million due in July. Formal creditor talks had not restarted after negotiations ended without agreement in April.

The tariff increase improves revenue potential but falls short of the 45% sought by the company. A further 15% rise proposed for January 2027 has not been approved. An earlier restructuring plan called for a 20% reduction in principal, an extension to 2033, scheduled amortization and coupons that would rise over time, with recoveries partly linked to freight volumes. Declining traffic, infrastructure attacks and higher labor, energy and repair costs remain the principal constraints on a revised deal.

Brazilian steelmaker CSN reported a 10th consecutive quarterly loss while pursuing asset sales and maturity relief. Its adjusted Q2 loss reached 773 million reais, almost six times the year-earlier amount, and net debt rose to 42.1 billion reais, or 3.49 times earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization. Bondholders approved a $1 billion exchange, and potential buyers submitted bids for the cement operation, but the higher leverage showed that those measures had not yet repaired the balance sheet.

## Local Funding Changes Create New Buyers and New Constraints

Several emerging markets altered the structure of domestic financing rather than simply changing policy rates. Vietnam exposed the most immediate imbalance: dong loans exceeded deposits by about 2 quadrillion dong, or $76.8 billion, as the government pressed banks to support double-digit economic growth.

The State Bank of Vietnam warned that the funding gap created risks for liquidity, interest rates and financial stability. Prime Minister Le Minh Hung nevertheless called for policy rates to remain unchanged, more market liquidity, lower bank funding costs and genuine reductions in lending rates. Banks have also been instructed to offer qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises loans at least 1 percentage point below each lender’s average rate for the same maturity.

The competing demands are becoming harder to reconcile. The government seeks almost 12% growth in the second half to reach its full-year objective, while July consumer inflation was 4.45% and early-year trade deficits increased demand for foreign currency. The central bank targets credit growth of about 15% but said room for monetary support was limited by inflation, external volatility and lenders’ funding capacity. Techcombank’s launch of a $1 billion syndicated loan underscored the turn toward offshore funding.

Nigeria widened the investor base for central-bank open-market securities to individuals, companies and non-bank financial institutions as well as banks. It also resumed 4- to 90-day repo operations and removed limits on access to the discount window for participants in foreign-exchange and government-bond auctions. The framework took effect immediately, with future OMO volumes and maturities dependent on liquidity and policy objectives.

Opening the instruments to the same pool of buyers as Treasury bills is expected by Rand Merchant Bank to compress OMO yields and narrow their spread to bill rates over time. It also gives domestic investors another yield-bearing alternative to equities. The change combines a broader channel for absorbing central-bank paper with restored flexibility to inject liquidity through term repos.

Sri Lanka continued moving in the opposite maturity direction, reducing reliance on foreign borrowing and short-dated domestic bills while increasing longer-term local bonds. Deputy Finance Minister Anil Jayantha Fernando said revenue was running approximately 15% above plan and the government remained on track to meet its 2026 deficit objective, although currency depreciation was raising expenditure. Officials were also considering eventual issuance of floating-rate, inflation-linked and green bonds.

Chile was creating a substantial new buyer for corporate debt. The public pension-support fund FAPP expects to raise about $4 billion over 5 years and $14 billion by 2036, with roughly two-thirds directed toward Chilean corporate fixed income. The allocation is large relative to a local company-bond market of about 102 trillion pesos, or $112 billion.

Private pension assets were also rising as higher employer contributions under the 2025 reform took effect. Assets increased by 35.2 trillion pesos in the 12 months through June to 234.4 trillion pesos. FAPP itself held 377.9 billion pesos as of March, all in fixed-income securities, and expects corporate bonds eventually to replace most of its sovereign allocation. The prospective demand offers local issuers a structural source of funding rather than a temporary response to the daily rates move.

Indonesia’s central-bank appointments similarly supported continuity while leaving the fiscal test unresolved. President Prabowo Subianto nominated Deputy Governor Aida S. Budiman for senior deputy governor and executive directors Solikin M. Juhro and M. Anwar Bashori for deputy-governor roles, after choosing acting Governor Destry Damayanti as the sole candidate to lead Bank Indonesia.

The selection of career officials reduced uncertainty after Perry Warjiyo’s departure, and the 10-year government yield fell 2 basis points to a 1-month low in early Thursday trading. Parliamentary approval is still required, with hearings expected to begin next week. The appointments do not settle how the central bank will balance rupiah stability against the administration’s demand for faster growth, particularly after legislation expanded its mandate to include sustainable economic development.

## Forward Market Significance

The Fed’s next test is whether July’s producer-price relief survives the remaining data before the September meeting. Core PCE is due Aug. 26, with economists at several banks projecting a 0.2% monthly increase. Its service components will determine whether lower energy, freight and trade margins were accompanied by sufficiently broad moderation. Additional employment reports must also show whether July’s hiring weakness was persistent or temporary.

Warsh’s Jackson Hole remarks later in August will determine how the Fed combines that evidence. A defense of July’s hold that emphasizes cumulative improvement would reinforce the reduction in September hike expectations. Greater weight on inflation still running above target, technology-related price pressure or the risk of waiting would preserve Hammack’s case even after the Treasury rally. The market is no longer certain of any increase this year, leaving communication capable of moving both the September probability and the December path.

Oil remains the most immediate external challenge to the disinflation narrative. Thursday’s 2.33% fall in WTI and 2.10% decline in Brent helped reduce near-term pressure, but the US and Iran had not reached terms restoring normal Strait of Hormuz traffic. Sustained vessel passage and lower freight and insurance costs would make July’s energy and transport declines more durable. Renewed attacks, continued disruption or another crude rally would restore the channel through which energy affects producer costs, breakevens and central-bank decisions.

Treasury’s auction cycle has cleared, but the financing question remains. The 30-year sale showed adequate demand at 5.216%, not evidence that investors would absorb the same duration at materially lower yields. Any future change in auction sizes must be assessed against the total borrowing requirement, the widening fiscal deficit and the amount of supply shifted into shorter maturities. The one-month steepening of 2s30s by 25.1 basis points leaves the long end sensitive to both budget policy and the next inflation reversal.

Japan’s Sept. 18 decision is the clearest overseas policy event. Government support for a near-term increase, 7.2% producer inflation and a yen near 160 all strengthen the case for action. The remaining issue is whether the BOJ describes one move as sufficient or signals a faster path capable of narrowing the rate differential more durably. Weak household spending and the risk of overtightening remain the counterweight.

Indonesia’s Aug. 14 budget speech is the more immediate Asian sovereign test. Investors will look for a credible deficit within the legal 3% ceiling and financing terms consistent with fiscal discipline. A deficit below 2.5% would be viewed favorably; CIMB estimates that a 2.2% deficit could lower net 2027 bond issuance to 722 trillion rupiah even as gross sales rise 1.4% to 1.75 quadrillion rupiah because of heavier maturities. Revenue assumptions, the cost of the free-meals program and any use of state-bank balance sheets will determine whether the plan supports the recent improvement in Indonesian bonds.

For corporate credit, the question is whether AI financing remains concentrated among issuers with strong cash and contractual backing or begins to reprice the wider high-grade market more aggressively. AMD’s $4.75 billion sale tightened during marketing, and Zenith Arc brought a long Jane Street lease to the project-bond market. The next transactions will test whether those features continue to offset the expanding volume of conventional debt, secured bonds and uncommenced lease obligations.

Stressed borrowers face more specific deadlines. Telesat must refinance or restructure its December maturities without relying on cash flow that its GEO business does not produce. Ukrainian Railways must convert the 30% freight increase into a creditor proposal after missing interest and principal payments, while the unapproved additional tariff increase leaves future revenue conditional. In both cases, new money has bought time or improved the operating base, but final debt terms and loss allocation remain unresolved.

section_summaries.summary: Japanese government support, 7.2% producer inflation and a yen near 160 strengthened the case for a BOJ increase in September or October, although timing remained undecided and weak household spending constrained the path. Norway held rates while retaining a tightening option, Turkey raised its inflation forecast while maintaining de facto restraint, and Australia found that falling home prices were tightening financial conditions.

section_summaries.summary: AMD’s $4.75 billion sale and Zenith Arc’s $2.25 billion project bond showed that investors would finance both strong technology borrowers and contract-backed data centers. The expanding supply and roughly $1 trillion of uncommenced hyperscaler lease obligations are beginning to reprice some defensive high-grade names, while Telesat, Ukrainian Railways and CSN still face unresolved refinancing or restructuring pressure.

section_summaries.market_read: Domestic financing reforms are changing who absorbs local debt and where liquidity pressure appears, even without policy-rate moves.
section_summaries.next_check: Indonesia’s Aug. 14 budget must pair credible revenue assumptions with a deficit inside the legal 3% ceiling.
section_summaries.section_title: Local Funding Changes Create New Buyers and New Constraints
section_summaries.summary: Vietnam’s loan-deposit gap exposed the tension between rapid credit growth and funding stability, while Nigeria broadened access to central-bank securities and restored term-repo flexibility. Sri Lanka shifted toward longer local debt, Chile’s pension-support fund created a prospective structural buyer for corporate bonds, and Indonesia’s career appointments reduced uncertainty without resolving the fiscal-policy test.

The Treasury rally depends on broader inflation moderation, continued relief in oil and freight costs, and Fed communication that validates waiting. Long-duration yields remain vulnerable to fiscal supply, while Japan’s Sept. 18 decision will test whether the BOJ intends a single increase or a faster tightening path. New AI debt and stressed refinancing negotiations will separately test the limits of credit demand.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally on softer producer prices, but the long bond still clears at a 25-year-high yield
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries ended Aug. 13 higher across the curve: the 2-year yield fell 5.9 basis points to 4.143%, the 5-year declined 6.6 basis points to 4.317%, the 10-year eased 5.1 basis points to 4.644% and the 30-year dropped 4.5 basis points to 5.215%. July producer prices were unchanged on the month and rose 4.7% from a year earlier, down from 5.5% in June, while core prices increased 0.2% and 4.2%. Falling energy, food and transportation costs pushed the implied probability of a September Fed increase below 40%.

The rally chiefly reflected a reassessment of the expected real policy and growth path: the 10-year real yield fell 4.5 basis points, while the breakeven slipped only 0.6 basis point. Lower oil prices reinforced that reading, although sharp increases in some service and technology-equipment prices kept the inflation picture mixed.

Treasury’s $25 billion 30-year auction stopped at 5.216%, the highest borrowing rate for such a sale since 2001, but its small tail and 2.39 bid-to-cover ratio showed demand remained available. The result was an orderly auction at a historically costly yield, leaving the long end exposed to deficits and financing supply even as softer inflation reduced immediate Fed pressure.
overall_summary.summary: Softer July producer inflation reduced expectations for near-term Fed tightening and pulled yields lower across the curve, but the $25 billion 30-year auction still required 5.216%, preserving the premium for duration, fiscal risk and heavy financing needs.
